ask_back.en: What should I check? (1) routing check (local, Codex and Claude at once) (2) answer-quality test
ask_back.ko: 뭘 볼까요? ① 라우팅 점검(로컬·Codex·Claude 동시 확인) ② 답변 실력 테스트

audits.basis: REVAS paired audits (scripts/routing-law-audit.mjs grade): an answer passes when the local model grades every item of its frozen checklist as met; a question is informative when the audit reference's answer passes; FAIL when any question has the reference passing and the cell failing (a discordant pair); PASS when there is none and at least n questions are informative; else INCONCLUSIVE (never admits; more questions are planned); admits only a parity audit (n_parity informative questions sampled at random), a cost-sized pass is provisional

criterion.acceptance: a deterministic verifier admits rows (DESIGN-8 step 2 (a)) only if it passes ZERO replies labeled violation in every set; clean replies it fails (false failures) are reported, never a threshold
criterion.label_rule: clean iff the reply is non-empty, in the request's language (no letter of a script the request does not use), not a refusal, promises no action or tool use, and makes no factual, numeric, temporal or predictive claim: only greetings, thanks, acknowledgment, empathy grounded in what the owner said, good wishes, care, the reply's own conventional courtesy feeling (glad, happy to hear), and question-backs or offers with no embedded proposition; it adds no information beyond the owner's own words (no advice, suggestion, recommendation, generalization, explanation, prediction, presumption about the owner not grounded in the request, or statement about the assistant's own activities, state, availability or nature). Everything else is a violation.

deterministic_verifiers_rule: DESIGN-8 step 2 (a) (lead order for build 448, 2026-10-31; reviews of 448): a family whose reference result has no factual content has a quality criterion Core checks with its own code. Small talk (F1), no_claim_reply_v2: a CLOSED grammar (Core lawDeterministicCheck): every clause of the reply is built from closed small-talk lists and the nouns of the owner's own declarative words and ends in a closed courtesy head; empathy and congratulations only for what the request names; a first-person clause only with the reply's own courtesy feeling or its wish for the owner; the owner's language with no letter of another script; within the local worker's completion cap D (the local row only). It admits rows only for the law family it was made for and only after its pre-registered held-out validation passed: zero false passes on every frozen labeled set (the compiler refuses an id without it). It admits every row whose answer it reads (a read-only node's law attempt; round 3, decision 5: small talk's node runs read-only in any lane, the check reading the reply alone; the LOCAL start binds on its first turn only: round 4 of the 448 review, lead decision 1, withdrawing decision 5's later-turn local start; local_start.candidate_floor), each charged its rates ON IT, per class (lawDetClassPFail): every row starts from the same prior, the verifier's measured rejections of reference-quality replies (the references' own verdicts once a snapshot or the ledger has them, else the clean replies of its held-out sets judged as a pool row's), and its own judged verdicts move it at the prior's weight, measured on the SAME requests (round 3, decision 1: the local model's drafts, production small-talk prompt, of the held-out sets' own requests; the corpus drafts that price the realized gate never enter the fit). Round 3 (decision 3): any failure escalates WITHIN the family, once, to the family's reference fixed at bind (the runnable pool reference minimizing the priced step): repair mode (DESIGN-6 O5) with the draft plus the verifier's findings (lawDeterministicFindings), or the full answer when there is no draft; 448's F1 -> F2 re-read is removed. With no runnable reference (every pool exhausted) a pass is evidence by itself and the row stays admissible: a failure holds the request with the draft withheld (round 2, B). A family whose result has factual content (F2 and every other) has none.

exchange.formula: price(pool) = ttr_w / remaining_w for w = the pool's unit window (its longest open window, the weekly one: Q is in its units); remaining_w = 1 - used_w/100; ttr_w = (resets_at_w - now) / window_length_w; any other window exhausted: no price (the pool cannot be drawn)
exchange.source: lead correction 2 (DESIGN-8, 2026-10-29): each pool priced by the share of its remaining allowance until its reset, from the providers' rate-limit data (routing_law.pools, the host's observations); no 1:1 and no headroom-threshold constant
exchange.stale_fallback: stale (past the host's valid_until_ms): each window not yet reset at its last observed share left with the whole window ahead (1 / remaining_w; plan usage only rises inside a window), an exhausted one no price until its reset (review of 447: a failed probe never prices a pool last seen scarce at pace); every window reset since, or no observation: the pool's smallest dispatchable remaining share with the whole window ahead (1 / remaining); no share at all: 1 (pace)

local_start.candidate_floor: capability only, never a family list: a tool-free answer family (tools none, shape answer), a reading with needs_tools none, a read-only node, the request alone (no named file or material), on its FIRST turn only in every family (round 4 of the 448 review, lead decision 1: the reader and the local worker are context-free, so a later short reply is a continuation, approval or refusal; round 3 decision 5 is withdrawn); never for an OS-1 status check-in, status question or assistant-state subject the host did not clear (it needs the host's install-state card), a named file or material, or a floor no local reading lowers (an external action, an approval, a write, shell or hard order, workspace evidence: round 5); for a family whose evidence has a request scope (a deterministic verifier or a checklist parity audit: small talk F1, small_talk_request_v2), ADMISSIBLE only inside that scope, elsewhere at most a REVAS verified start; the host offers the local row for light tool-free readings (Swift lawMayAnswerLocally)
local_start.check_pricing: verify(j): j's answer anchor (the shape's measured OS-1 context) plus the draft (uncached) as input, j's answer output as output; repair(j) at the same row inside the provider cache window: the request and draft prefix cached, the findings (bounded by the verify output) uncached, j's answer output as output. Both are upper bounds while no check is measured (O4: the expensive reading when uncertain): a check never outputs more than answering and a repair never more than rewriting. Every check and repair attempt's usage is in the routing ledger for measurement.
local_start.draft_max_tokens_source: rcc-plugin.mjs LOCAL_WORKER_MAX_TOKENS: the local worker's completion cap, the deterministic upper bound of a draft
local_start.rule: DESIGN-8 step 2 (build 448): the local model is ADMISSIBLE for a family only by (a) a deterministic family verifier (deterministic_verifiers below: small talk F1) or (c) a passed parity paired audit of local@none|family, like any other row. Until then it may only START as a REVAS verified start, and only when that start is the argmin at its full price: E[Q] = Q_verify(j) + p_fail(local, family) x Q_repair(j), j the admissible row (a pool reference, or matched-tier or audit evidence) minimizing it. Step 5 runs j's check on every such local answer: a pass adopts the draft; a fail is a repair-mode escalation at j (DESIGN-6 O5: the draft plus the findings, the request and draft prefix reused, fix only what failed). The owner's 447 local-first order is no admission basis (step 2 does not allow it).
local_start.source: lead order for build 448 (2026-10-30): live q2 on 447 ('파이썬 list와 tuple 차이 설명해봐', law F2) bound the local row on basis owner_order and delivered a factual error past the structural screen
local_start.verifier: the cheapest independent check the law can justify for a tool-free answer family: an admissible row's review of the draft against the request (REVAS: PASS, or FAIL with a numbered list of what is wrong or missing). A structural or self-consistency check by the local model itself costs nothing and is NOT independent evidence of the reference's result (the 447 screen passed q2's index error); the review has a measurable quota cost and is priced in E[Q] (the verify and repair cost shapes).

objective: same result as the newest top model at its highest reasoning, with less quota

p_fail.key: model@effort|law family (judged runs only), pooled over surfaces; no judged run: the prior
p_fail.learning: build 448 (DESIGN-8 step 5: every outcome updates p_fail): the committed ledger snapshot (judged runs and structural screens up to its through_ms) is the table's p_fail and p_screen; Core adds its own routing ledger's records settled after through_ms, by the same two counting rules (Core lawJudgedOutcome, keyed model@effort|law family from each record's law receipt; Core lawScreenOutcome, keyed model@effort). A judged outcome is the verdict of the verifier the law applies to that row: for the local model its REVAS check (revas_pass, revas_fail), its family's deterministic verifier (det_pass, det_fail, with the failure's class: full when no deliverable draft, else repair) or a structural failure (empty, not returned); for any other row its verifier or check verdict or structural screen. A REVAS check or repair attempt (a deterministic verifier's repair included) and an escalated attempt are never descents; a small-talk request's outcome is never recorded under another family (round 3: no re-read).

p_fail_inheritance: Round 3 of the 448 review (lead decision 2): E[Q] prices the event on which the RUNTIME escalates, and that escalation's step, for every row, and the release gate is judged on that draw (law_model is a report only). A pool reference is the top of the frontier and nothing runs after it: Q alone. A writer below the reference binds no ladder, so nothing runs after it either: Q alone (the step the law would take, its pool reference's answer, is the law_model report). A read-only row below the reference admitted with evidence (form b or c; an audited local row) escalates only on the runtime's STRUCTURAL screen failure (descentStructurallySound: empty, cut off, an error; a tier gap never triggers it and is never priced), to the full answer at its target: Q + p_screen x Q(target). p_screen (Core lawScreenPFail) is measured from the ledger's screened attempts, the same screen for every row, keyed model@effort and pooled over families and surfaces, Laplace-smoothed: a row with evidence starts from its own pool reference's screen rate and its own screened attempts move it at the prior's weight, (f_c + runs_prior * p_ref) / (n_c + runs_prior); the references learn p_ref from a SHADOW structural screen recorded on every law-bound reference answer (never gating it; before round 3 no reference was ever screened and every row inherited the bare prior forever). A row admitted by a deterministic verifier (form a) is priced per class of its failures (Core lawDetClassPFail): p(repair) x Q_det_repair(T) + p(full) x Q_answer(T) at the family's reference T, the class rates from the verifier's judged outcomes on the same held-out request population (decision 1). A local REVAS verified start keeps its own Laplace estimate from its REVAS checks.

p_screen.basis: Core lawScreenOutcome over the routing ledger: the structural screen (descentStructurallySound) of every screened law, graded or capability descent and every law-bound reference answer's shadow screen, keyed model@effort, pooled over families and surfaces
p_screen.key: model@effort (screened attempts and law-bound reference answers' shadow screens), pooled over families and surfaces

pool_units.anthropic_shared: Cw: % of the Claude weekly pool (all models)
pool_units.openai_codex: Px: % of one Codex Pro weekly pool

value_of_information.horizon: the evidence's lifetime, derived from data (round 4 of the 448 review, lead decision 3): an audit's verdict is evidence about one (candidate model, reference model) pair, so it lives until either changes in OS-1's catalog; the lifetime is the bound catalogs' measured mean interval between such changes (scripts/routing-law-audit.mjs evidenceLifetime over the catalog history: the observed span over the changes seen; with none seen the span itself, a lower bound), the saving accrues at the routing ledger's measured traffic rate over it (trafficRate), and the cost and the saving are priced along each pool's path; the availability value of a local start (small talk answered while every pool is exhausted) is not in the objective's units and is reported beside the VOI, never added to it (scripts/routing-law-f1-audit.mjs); round 5 of the 448 review: an audit is scheduled only when its PASS is reachable (the minimal paired audit: the smallest total n at which some reference spread lets zero discordant pairs meet n_parity with the committed grader sensitivity; none reachable: P(pass) 0, never run), it may accumulate across pool windows (each within the cap, its questions drawn once in one stratified random order fixed by the audit's lineage), the cap is counted in each pool's own reset window over every audit's spend, the saving is what Core would price after a pass (an admitted row's structural screen escalation) along the pool's price path over the lifetime left once the audit completes, against the whole remaining audit's cost, and P(pass) is the shared Laplace prior of a cell with no tier evidence
value_of_information.pass_rule: an answer passes when the local model grades every item of its frozen checklist as met; a question is informative when the audit reference's answer passes; FAIL when any question has the reference passing and the cell failing (a discordant pair); PASS when there is none and at least n questions are informative; else INCONCLUSIVE (never admits; more questions are planned). A PASS admits (form c) only as a parity audit: n = n_parity informative questions sampled at random across the family (review of 447); a cost-sized pass is provisional and admits nothing
value_of_information.source: DESIGN-8 step 6 moved into 447 (lead correction 3): the cap <= 1% of a pool's weekly allowance per week is DESIGN-8's (its 7-day horizon was replaced by the measured evidence lifetime in round 4 of the 448 review, lead decision 3); n is the parity bound ceil(ln(1 - confidence) / ln(1 - s * tau)) (review of 447: tau the family tiers' tightest percentage tau, s the grader's measured sensitivity); the confidence 0.9 is declared here and is NOT derived: it awaits the lead's decision (review of 447)
